portName: Port of Bar (Bar Cruise Port, Port of Adria)
townName: Bar town centre and Stari Bar
seoTitle: Bar cruise port guide: shuttle, promenade and Stari Bar
seoDescription: Bar cruise ships berth inside the Port of Adria; a shuttle bus runs to King Nikola's Promenade. Stari Bar is 4 km inland, about €5 by taxi (2026).
quickAnswer: Ships berth alongside at the Port of Adria cruise quays on the western edge of Bar, inside a secure port area, and shuttle buses take passengers to the start of King Nikola's Promenade in the centre. Stari Bar, the ruined old town, is 4 km inland: about €5 by taxi (2026). Be at the shuttle stop at least 75 minutes before all-aboard so you are on board 60 minutes before.
intro: Bar is Montenegro's main commercial port, a modern town spread along a bay with a palm-lined promenade. Cruise ships use two berths in the Port of Adria, the privatised part of the port run with Global Ports Holding. The berths are inside a working port, and in 2026 the town ran shuttle buses from the port to the start of King Nikola's Promenade. Most visitors come for Stari Bar, a walled medieval town abandoned in the late 19th century and now a large ruin field at the foot of Mount Rumija, and for an olive tree said to be 2,000 years old or more. Budva and Sveti Stefan are up the coast; this guide could not confirm a usable public bus timetable, so take the ship's tour if you want to go.

terminals.name: Bar Cruise Port (Port of Adria, two cruise berths)
terminals.notes: Global Ports Holding places the port on the western edge of Bar, with two cruise berths of 290 m and 200 m (490 m in all) for ships up to 330 m. There is no terminal building yet; one is planned. Global Ports Holding lists a shuttle service. Its fact sheet gives 'City Center: 50m', but the cruise berths are inside a secure port and passengers are taken by shuttle bus to the start of King Nikola's Promenade, so do not plan on a 50 m walk. Local press reported 30 buses shuttling passengers from the port to the promenade on a busy day in April 2026.

walkability.detail: Take the port shuttle bus from the ship to the start of King Nikola's Promenade. No cruise line or port source gives a walking route or time out of the Port of Adria, and the berths are inside a restricted area. Once at the promenade, central Bar is flat and walkable: King Nikola's Palace and its gardens are along the waterfront, and Šušanj beach is further north along the promenade. Stari Bar is 4 km inland and uphill; Global Ports Holding calls it about an hour's walk up, so take a taxi.

transportSections.cost: Not confirmed; check your daily programme
transportSections.detail: Runs from the cruise berth through the port area to the stop at the start of King Nikola's Promenade. The return to the ship is from the same stop. Global Ports Holding lists a shuttle service at the port.

Take one from the centre near the promenade. Use only licensed taxis and confirm the fare before setting off. A good plan is to ride up and walk down the cobbled street below the walls to find a taxi back.

Intercity buses run along the coast, but this guide could not confirm a timetable or where they leave from relative to the shuttle stop. Summer traffic on the coast road is heavy. Take the ship's tour, which the ship waits for.

returnTiming.rule: Be at the shuttle stop at the start of King Nikola's Promenade at least 75 minutes before all-aboard, so you are back on board 60 minutes before. Leave Stari Bar at least 90 minutes before all-aboard.
returnTiming.detail: The shuttle ride time and frequency were not confirmed, and on busy days several ships share the shuttle, so allow for a queue. From Stari Bar the taxi to the centre takes about 10 minutes, but taxis can be scarce when tours finish. Do not try to walk into the port.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Go to the shuttle stop at the start of King Nikola's Promenade and phone the port agent number on your daily programme. Ship's tours have the ship wait for them; independent travellers do not.

diyVsExcursion.ship: From US$99.99 adult for the Old Bar & Bar Walking Tour, 3.5 hours (Norwegian Cruise Line, 2026); Princess sells an 'Old Bar On Your Own' transfer from US$64.95
diyVsExcursion.diy: Shuttle, then a taxi of about €5 each way plus the Stari Bar entrance fee (2026)

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Not recommended: no usable bus timetable confirmed

excursionAdvice: Do Stari Bar on your own: it is a 10-minute taxi ride from the centre, and the ship's walking tour costs far more than the taxi and ticket. Budva and Sveti Stefan are the case for a tour. The journey is long, summer traffic on the coast road is slow, and the ship waits for its own tours. Note that Sveti Stefan island is reserved for Aman resort guests; tours stop at a viewpoint.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00, all-aboard is 17:30 and a summer day. Sun Princess's first 2026 call ran 07:00 to 18:00.

steps.what: Take the port shuttle bus to the start of King Nikola's Promenade.
Take a licensed taxi from the centre to Stari Bar, about €5.
Enter Stari Bar (summer opening from 08:00). Walk the wall near the entrance for the aqueduct view, then loop through the ruins.
Coffee or fresh pomegranate juice on the cobbled street below the walls.
Taxi to the old olive tree in Mirovica, €1 entry.
Lunch on or near the promenade.
Walk to King Nikola's Palace and its gardens, then along the promenade to Šušanj beach.
Walk back along the promenade to the shuttle stop.
Take the shuttle bus back to the ship, 75 minutes before all-aboard.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Stari Bar (Old Bar)
sights.why: A walled medieval town at the foot of Mount Rumija, abandoned in the late 19th century, with ruined churches, Turkish baths, a stone mosque and fortress walls.
sights.cost: Entrance fee paid at the gate; carry euro cash
sights.tip: Open about 08:00–20:00 in summer and 09:00–17:00 in winter. Paths are uneven cobbles with steep steps and little shade; go early and take water and a hat.

sights.name: Stari Bar aqueduct
sights.why: A large Ottoman-era stone aqueduct on the north side of the old town.
sights.cost: Seen from the walls with the Stari Bar ticket
sights.tip: Look for it from the city walls near the entrance.

sights.name: Old olive tree (Stara Maslina), Mirovica
sights.why: An olive tree estimated to be at least 2,000 years old.
sights.tip: Combine with Stari Bar; it is between the old town and the new town.

sights.name: King Nikola's Palace
sights.why: Palace built in 1885 by King Nikola for his daughter Princess Zorka; it now houses Bar's town museum and hosts concerts and exhibitions.
sights.tip: In a park of palms and rare plants by the waterfront, along the promenade.

sights.name: King Nikola's Promenade
sights.why: A wide, flat palm-lined waterfront walk with cafés and restaurants, where the port shuttle drops you.
sights.tip: Follow it north to the palace and Šušanj.

sights.name: Šušanj beach
sights.why: The town's main pebble beach, north of the centre along the promenade.
sights.tip: About 15–25 minutes on foot from the centre.

beaches.name: Šušanj
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk north along the promenade from the shuttle stop
beaches.time: About 15–25 minutes on foot from the centre
beaches.note: Pebble beach north of the centre.

beaches.name: Sutomore
beaches.time: About 8 km from Bar; TUI puts it under 15 minutes' drive
beaches.cost: Free; sunbeds, snacks and drinks for sale
beaches.note: Long mixed pebble and sand beach; busy in summer.

food.where: Cafés on the cobbled street up to Stari Bar

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to walk out of the port.
commonMistakes.fix: The berths are inside a secure port. Take the shuttle bus to the start of King Nikola's Promenade.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trusting the '50 m to the centre' figure.
commonMistakes.fix: That is the port operator's fact sheet, not the walk from the ship. Allow for the shuttle in both directions.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to walk to Stari Bar in the heat.
commonMistakes.fix: It is 4 km uphill, about an hour on foot. Take a taxi up for about €5.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning Budva or Sveti Stefan by public bus.
commonMistakes.fix: No usable timetable was confirmed and summer coast traffic is heavy. Take the ship's tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Getting into an unlicensed taxi without agreeing the price.
commonMistakes.fix: Use licensed taxis and confirm the fare first.
The ruins are uneven cobbles and steep steps. Wear shoes with grip.

safety: Bar is generally safe for visitors. GOV.UK advises watching bags and phones in busy tourist areas, beaches and on public transport. The main practical risks are heat and uneven ground at Stari Bar, and traffic: drivers do not always stop at crossings, and pedestrians can be fined for crossing within 100 m of a marked crossing without using it. At the beach, follow flags and lifeguards and swim in marked areas, as speedboats are common in summer. Wildfires are common from April to October.
scams: Taxi overcharging: some drivers overcharge tourists. Use licensed taxis and agree the fare before you go.
Card skimming: card details can be stolen at street ATMs or when paying. Use ATMs inside banks and keep your card in sight.
accessibility: The berths are inside the port, so plan on the shuttle bus; ask the ship about step-free shuttle access. The promenade and town centre are flat, and the palace gardens are on level ground. Stari Bar is not suitable for wheelchair users: the paths are uneven cobblestones with steep stairs. The promenade is the best step-free option.
rainyDay: Stari Bar's cobbles become slippery in rain, so go carefully or skip it. King Nikola's Palace and the town museum are the indoor option, followed by cafés on the promenade.
crowdTips: Bar can take several ships in a few days; on 21 April 2026 the town used 30 shuttle buses and 52 excursion coaches. Stari Bar fills with tour groups by mid-morning, so go early, and expect a queue at the shuttle stop late in the afternoon.

faqs.q: Is Bar walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Not directly. The berths are inside the Port of Adria, and a shuttle bus takes you to the start of King Nikola's Promenade. From there the centre is flat and walkable.

faqs.q: Is there a shuttle from Bar cruise port to the town?
faqs.a: Yes. Shuttle buses run from the port to the start of King Nikola's Promenade. Check your daily programme for times and any charge.

faqs.q: How do I get from Bar cruise port to Stari Bar?
faqs.a: Take the shuttle to the promenade, then a licensed taxi of about 10 minutes, about €5 one way (2026).
No. Ships berth alongside at two cruise quays, 290 m and 200 m long.

faqs.q: Can I visit Budva from Bar cruise port?
faqs.a: Take the ship's tour. This guide could not confirm a usable public bus timetable, and summer coast traffic is heavy.

faqs.q: Can you visit Sveti Stefan island?
faqs.a: Not unless you are staying there. The Aman resort reopened on 1 July 2026 and the island is for guests only; you can view it from the coast.
Šušanj is a pebble beach north of the centre along the promenade. Sutomore, about 8 km north, is larger.
Yes. Watch your belongings in busy areas, use licensed taxis and take care crossing roads.
